public_rationale: Both parts hold. Part 1: the Sun Yat-sen/Alibaba SWE-CI paper Marcus cites tested 18 models. It reports that within each provider family, newer models always scored higher, with markedly larger gains for models released after 2026. Part 2 is a claim about what can happen, and it is well documented. GAO found that a Patriot missile battery at Dhahran failed to intercept a Scud because of one software problem in its weapons control computer: a tracking error that grew over time. The Scud killed 28 Americans. Leveson and Turner's investigation of the Therac-25 radiation machine ties massive overdoses, with deaths, partly to software errors. These cases involve conventional software, not AI. The claim only says such errors can be deadly, so this grade does not judge the Amazon comparison that follows it.
limitations: Part 1 rests on one preprint benchmark.
Part 2 is a general possibility, shown with historical non-AI cases.
The Therac-25 accidents had several causes, not software alone.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Some of the latest AI coding systems have done better than earlier ones, but in mission-critical systems even a small number of errors can be deadly.

statement.excerpt: In fairness, some of the latest systems have done better than earlier ones, but for mission critical systems, even a small number of errors can be deadly.
statement.document_title: “A spate of outages, including incidents tied to the use of AI coding tools”, right on schedule

from_speaker: some of the latest systems have done better than earlier ones
even a small number of errors can be deadly
our_interpretation: Part 1: on the long-term maintainability benchmark he cites (SWE-CI, Sun Yat-sen University and Alibaba), at least some newer AI coding systems scored better than earlier ones as of the post date.

Part 2 is a possibility claim ('can be'). It holds if documented cases exist where a small number of software errors in a mission-critical system contributed to deaths. It does not claim that AI-written code has killed anyone, and the Amazon aside in the next sentence is not graded here.
Part 1 describes results available at the post date (March 2026). Part 2 is a general claim covering history up to the post date.
criteria.support_condition: Part 1: the cited benchmark or similar evidence shows newer models scoring higher than earlier ones. Part 2: an official or scholarly accident investigation ties deaths to one or a few software errors in a safety- or mission-critical system.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Part 1: newer systems do no better than older ones on the cited benchmark. Part 2: no documented case exists of a small number of software errors causing deaths in a mission-critical system.

evidence.excerpt:
On February 25, 1991, a Patriot missile defense system operating at
Dhahran, Saudi Arabia, during Operation Desert Storm failed to track and
intercept an incoming Scud. This Scud subsequently hit an Army barracks,
killing 28 Americans.
evidence.publisher: US General Accounting Office (GAO), report IMTEC-92-26
evidence.explanation: An official GAO report records a failure in a mission-critical defense system that was followed by 28 deaths. Item e3 shows the cause was a software problem.

evidence.excerpt:
This problem led to an inaccurate tracking calculation that became
worse the longer the system operated.
evidence.publisher: US General Accounting Office (GAO), report IMTEC-92-26
evidence.explanation: GAO traced the failure to one software problem in the weapons control computer. This shows a small number of errors can be deadly in a mission-critical system.

evidence.excerpt: Six accidents involving massive overdoses to patients occurred between 1985 and 1987. The machine was recalled in 1987 for extensive design changes, including hardware safeguards against software errors.
evidence.publisher: IEEE Computer (Leveson and Turner, 1993), reprinted by MIT
evidence.explanation: A peer-reviewed investigation of a medical device whose software errors were tied to massive overdoses. The authors' introduction says these accidents caused deaths. The authors also stress that the accidents had multiple causes.
